title: Synthetic Study A: Compact-TiO2 MAPbI3 Perovskite Solar Cells with 21.1% Initial Efficiency

paragraphs.text: We report methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) that reach a certified power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.1% under 1-sun AM1.5G illumination at initial scan.
Perovskite solar cells have advanced rapidly, yet long-term operational stability remains the key barrier to commercialization.
Devices were fabricated on fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) glass substrates with a compact TiO2 electron transport layer deposited by spray pyrolysis.
The MAPbI3 absorber was deposited by a one-step spin-coating method, followed by spiro-OMeTAD as the hole transport layer and a gold electrode.
X-ray diffraction (XRD) confirmed a phase-pure tetragonal MAPbI3 film with no detectable PbI2 residue.
The champion device delivered a PCE of 21.1% with an open-circuit voltage of 1.12 V and a fill factor of 0.80 under 1-sun illumination.
Encapsulated devices retained 95% of their initial PCE after 200 h of shelf storage in the dark.
The hysteresis index was not measured in this study.
We attribute the high initial efficiency to the compact TiO2 layer, which suppresses interfacial recombination.
These results show that compact TiO2 based PSCs can combine high initial PCE with good shelf stability.
Current density-voltage curves were recorded with a masked aperture of 0.09 cm2.
